doublecortin like kinase-1 (Dclk-1) is not a marker of normal stem cells in intestinal tissue but instead is expressed by tumor stem cells in intestinal tumors, and that ablation of Dcl-1 positive tumor stem cells results in a marked regression in tumor size.
Dclk1 marks intestinal tumor stem cells (iTS) in the polyps, and specific ablation of iTS results in a marked regression in polyps without apparent intestinal damage.
Dclk1 distinguishes TSCs from NSCs, and that Dclk1 is a promising candidate target for colorectal cancer therapy.

the identification of tumor stem cells (tumor-initiating cells) in colorectal cancer and the development of a therapy based on targeting these cells.
the identification and validation of a novel marker for tumor stem cells.
the identification of a marker of tumor stem cells in the gut.

DCLK1 expression marks TSCs in intestinal tumors and is not expressed by NSCs in the normal intestine.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Dclk1 is a TSC-specific marker and that a therapy based on Dclk1 may be a promising strategy for treating colorectal cancer.
Dclk1 is a marker for intestinal tumor stem cells, and that targeting Dclk1 could lead to effective treatment of colorectal cancer.
Dclk1 marks TSCs in intestinal adenomas, and that Dclk1-specific ablation results in regression of the adenomas without apparent damage to normal intestinal tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dclk1 is a marker of TSCs in the intestine and not of NSCs, as previously thought.
